background_incidence: 413 per 100,000 person-years (ages 2-4y) and 573 per 100,000 person-years (ages 5-15y) in Pakistan; cited from Ochiai et al. 2008 five-Asian-country burden study (ref 5)
outbreak_frequency: MDR S Typhi endemic in Pakistan/south Asia since 1980s; fluoroquinolone resistance emerged over past two decades, rising 84.7%->91.7% in a 2009-11 national review, >90% of south Asian isolates now reduced ciprofloxacin susceptibility; ceftriaxone/cefixime resistance <1% in 2009-14 Pakistan data; ceftriaxone-resistant XDR H58 clone first identified Nov 30, 2016, ~100 cases by Mar 2017, 486 cases by Dec 30, 2017
endemicity: Stated as endemic: "healthy controls were selected in areas where typhoid fever is endemic and common"; Asia contributes 90% of global typhoid morbidity/mortality
seasonality: NA - no seasonal pattern stated; epidemic curve (Nov 2016-Dec 2017) shows biweekly case peaks growing successively larger over time, consistent with a propagated (not seasonal) epidemic
notes: TCV (Typbar) mass campaign started Mar 2018 for ages 6mo-10y in affected areas, ~115,000 doses by Oct 2018; water chlorination and sewerage repair recommended

background_incidence: Typhoid "endemic in South Asia," most common bacteremic illness in children in Pakistan; rates as high as 1000 cases/100,000 child-years reported from Karachi.
outbreak_frequency: Ceftriaxone resistance previously rare: only 4 cases (0.01%) of ceftriaxone-resistant S. Typhi in Pakistan 2012-2015 (retrospective AKU lab surveillance); <1% ceftriaxone-resistant 2009-2012/2009-2014 in Karachi. XDR outbreak: 101 cases, 30 Nov 2016-28 Mar 2017 (~4 months), 2 subdistricts (Latifabad, Qasimabad); largest ceftriaxone-resistant S. Typhi outbreak reported worldwide.
endemicity: Endemic in South Asia; Pakistan described as high-disease-burden country for typhoid/AMR.
seasonality: NA
notes: Epidemic curve cyclical/irregular with 2 peaks, suggesting common-source + propagated transmission via contaminated water (sewage-line clustering, non-functioning sludge plants). TCV mass-vaccination pilot (children 6mo-10y) started last week of Jan 2018 in Hyderabad.

outbreak_frequency: Frequent common-source outbreaks reported in Myanmar since 1989; 4 major water-borne outbreaks in the decade to 2000; nearby Singaing township also had a typhoid outbreak

seasonality: Notifiable disease occurrence peaks June-August
notes: Recurrence driven by untreated Myaung River water, unsanitary latrines near riverbank, and heavy rain/flooding contaminating river; villages communicate daily enabling spread between townships

notes: National typhoid notifications declining overall; recurrence driven by unresolved unsafe water supply; suspected carrier(s) may sustain inter-outbreak circulation over 12 years

background_incidence: Pre-outbreak average incidence 1.8/100,000/year (5-yr average before outbreak); rose to 25.2/100,000 during 2009-2011 outbreak; Thailand overall regional incidence 0.9-83.6/100,000 (2013)
outbreak_frequency: Two related outbreaks: 1st Oct 2009-Mar 2010, 2nd Sep 2010-Jul 2011, separated by ~5-month remission (Apr-Aug 2010); 2nd wave larger than 1st; outbreak ended with cases returning to historical (endemic) norms
endemicity: Thailand endemic for typhoid; incidence low outside outbreaks but varies markedly by region and outbreak status
seasonality: No clear seasonal cycle reported; remission during Apr-May coincided with school summer break, not intrinsic seasonality
notes: PFGE showed same strain pattern across schools/months, suggesting common source; vaccination not used since source-control measures were expected to suffice

outbreak_frequency: SEFI pediatric cohort (~6,000 children, 4 urban settlements) under active surveillance Oct 2017-Dec 2019; outbreak (Apr-Jun 2019) detected as cases exceeding mean+2SD of surveillance counts in corresponding months of prior years 2017-2018, implying continuous sporadic/endemic transmission; no other prior outbreak explicitly described
endemicity: Described as typhoid-endemic setting with suboptimal WaSH; short- and long-cycle S. Typhi transmission; only 8.6% of cohort vaccinated
seasonality: Hot season Mar-Jul (May/June max temp 42C/39.2C 2019); majority of outbreak cases in May; water scarcity in summer proposed driver of seasonal surge
notes: Overall cohort attack rate 0.9% (outbreak period); ref.4 (John 2018) is the source SEFI/NSSEFI incidence paper, not detailed here; H58 lineage II S. Typhi
